config.title: Build CLS FID LCP web vitals logger

intro.title: Build CLS FID LCP web vitals logger
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a web vitals logger that tracks three key performance metrics: Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS), First Input Delay (FID), and Largest Contentful Paint (LCP). You will learn how to use the web-vitals JavaScript library to measure these metrics in a real browser environment. The core programming concept involves importing and using external modules, handling asynchronous data with event listeners, and logging results to the console. By the end, you will have a functional script that reports these vital performance scores, helping you understand user experience on web pages.
intro.usecase: This pattern is essential for performance monitoring dashboards in web applications, such as those used by engineering teams at companies like Netflix or Airbnb to track user experience. Developers implement Web Vitals loggers to capture CLS, FID, and LCP metrics in real-time, displaying them in admin panels or analytics tools to identify performance bottlenecks. For example, an e-commerce site might use this logger to alert when slow LCP affects product page load times, directly impacting sales. By learning this, you'll be equipped to build the backend data collection that powers these critical performance insights.

objectives: Initialize a web vitals monitoring script in a JavaScript project
Configure event listeners to capture CLS, FID, and LCP metric data
Construct a logging function that formats web vitals data for output
Implement data storage logic to persist vitals measurements locally
Integrate the vitals logger with a simple dashboard display
Manipulate the DOM to render real-time web vitals updates
Apply error handling to manage missing or invalid vitals data

steps.title: Define CLS logging function
steps.instruction: Define a function named logCLS that takes one parameter (metric) and logs the CLS value to the console.
steps.hint: Create a function that receives the metric object and logs metric.value to the console with a descriptive message.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named logCLS is defined that will handle CLS metric data from the web-vitals library.
successCriteria: The logCLS function is defined with one parameter and logs the metric value to console.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Define FID logging function
steps.instruction: Define a function named logFID that takes a single parameter (call it 'metric') and logs the FID value to the console.
steps.hint: Create a function that receives the metric parameter and uses console.log to output the FID value. The function should be similar to the CLS function but handle FID data.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a logFID function that logs FID metric data to the console.
successCriteria: A function named logFID is defined with a metric parameter and logs the FID value using console.log.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function is named logFID and takes a metric parameter. It should log the FID value to the console.

steps.title: Define LCP logging function
steps.instruction: Define a function named 'logLCP' that takes a 'metric' parameter and logs the LCP value with a descriptive message.
steps.hint: Follow the same pattern as the CLS and FID functions you created earlier. Use console.log to output the metric.value with an appropriate message.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named 'logLCP' that logs the LCP metric value when called.
successCriteria: The 'logLCP' function is defined with a 'metric' parameter and uses console.log to output the LCP value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started defining the LCP function, but make sure it takes a 'metric' parameter and logs the value with console.log.

steps.title: Initialize web vitals reporting in main function
steps.instruction: Inside the main function, call the web-vitals library functions to start reporting CLS, FID, and LCP metrics using your logging functions.
steps.hint: You'll need to call onCLS, onFID, and onLCP functions from the web-vitals library, passing your logging functions as callbacks.
steps.expectedOutcome: The main function now contains calls to web-vitals reporting functions that will trigger your logging functions when metrics are available.
successCriteria: The main function calls onCLS, onFID, and onLCP from the web-vitals library with logCLS, logFID, and logLCP as callbacks.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling all three web-vitals functions (onCLS, onFID, onLCP) with your corresponding logging functions.

successCriteria: The logCLS function contains console.log statements that display metric.name, metric.value, and metric.id.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Add timestamp to log output
steps.instruction: Modify the logCLS function to include a timestamp in its console output. Add a new console.log statement that logs the current timestamp along with the CLS value.
steps.hint: You can get the current timestamp using Date.now() or new Date().toISOString(). Add this inside the logCLS function before or after the existing console.log.
steps.expectedOutcome: The logCLS function will output both the CLS value and a timestamp when called, making debugging easier.
successCriteria: The logCLS function includes a console.log statement that outputs a timestamp along with the CLS value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
